basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 17-22.' and it opens 'VERS. 17-22.--Deinde venit in valle Geraris, et habitavit ibi. Pro valle torrentem habet'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 17-22.--Deinde venit in valle Geraris, et habitavit ibi. Pro valle torrentem habet in Hebraeo. Neque enim Isaac habitare poterat in valle. Habitavit autem in torrente, postquam magnus factus est. De quo scriptum est: De torrente in via bibet (Psal. CIX, 7). De quo etiam Elias bibit. Sed quia Elias non erat perfectus ut Christus, ideo torrens | ille aruit. Dominus vero noster etiam in torrente traditus est, dedicans regenerationem nostram et baptismi sacramentum.
